subject.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins

question: Which open branch should be the canonical fix for the npm metadata failure and destructive plugin-disablement issue?
rationale: Both this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 modify the same resolver-installer-updater contract, while this PR additionally changes the sibling update-check parser; selecting and consolidating one branch requires maintainer coordination.

options.title: Use this broader branch
options.body: Keep this PR as canonical after adding valid exact-head CLI state-transition proof, because it includes the shared failure-policy repair plus singleton-array handling in the sibling update checker.

options.title: Use the narrower branch
options.body: Select https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 and port the necessary update-check parser coverage before closing this PR as superseded.

options.title: Pause both branches
options.body: Hold both PRs if maintainers do not want all non-E404 pre-install metadata failures to preserve existing plugin state.

recommendation.title: Use this broader branch
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as canonical after adding valid exact-head CLI state-transition proof, because it includes the shared failure-policy repair plus singleton-array handling in the sibling update checker.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged history shows the strongest ownership signal across plugin update, install, and metadata-resolution behavior.
